reference: GNU grep -P is the oracle for portable PCRE line selection and extraction, and GNU sed -E is the oracle for the shared capture and global-substitution subset. PCRE-only capture-array, zero-width iteration, metadata, and binary -X expectations are explicit contracts derived from the loadable documentation, PCRE2 syntax, and manually encoded byte strings; no expectation is taken from candidate output.
coverage: Unicode named and numbered captures with an unset optional group
match failure clears previous BPCRE_MATCH captures
global substitution and per-line global capture substitution
find-all digit extraction and zero-width match advancement
grep across multiple fixture files, including filename prefixes and no-match status
binary NUL substitution through documented hex transport
malformed-pattern failure status and diagnostic presence
exclusions: The bounded cases do not qualify every PCRE flag, cache eviction, configurable match/depth limits, invalid UTF handling, or large-output behavior.
A live producer-open grep flush check is deferred because this runner has no producer-open FIFO or PTY observation hook; ordinary closed-input grep behavior is covered by parity cases.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports pcre as a builtin and help -d exposes the documented short description; this is availability metadata, not operation coverage.
cases.stdout:
builtin
pcre - Perl-compatible regex via libpcre2-8 (no JIT).

cases.purpose: Verify documented UTF/UCP text mode, named and numbered capture indexing, and an absent optional capture using a fixed PCRE2 pattern and subject.
Check the documented state transition that a validated non-match clears captures from an earlier successful match and returns failure for that match.
cases.script:
pcre match '(old)' old
if pcre match '(new)' old; then
  printf 'unexpected-match\n'
  exit 9
else
  rc=$?
fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
printf '%s\n' "${#BPCRE_MATCH[@]}"

cases.purpose: Compare global digit capture replacement on a single deterministic subject with GNU sed extended regular expressions.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t pcre) == builtin ]]; then
  pcre subst '([0-9]+)' '<$1>' 'id=12;id=34' -g
else
  printf '%s\n' 'id=12;id=34' | sed -E 's/([0-9]+)/<\1>/g'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare pcre sed's documented per-line global capture substitution with GNU sed -E on matching and unchanged fixture lines.
cases.script:
printf 'item-12 item-7\nkeep\n' > rows.txt
if [[ $(type -t pcre) == builtin ]]; then
  pcre sed '([a-z]+)-([0-9]+)' '<\1:\2>' rows.txt
else
  sed -E 's/([a-z]+)-([0-9]+)/<\1:\2>/g' rows.txt
fi

cases.purpose: Compare successive non-overlapping digit matches with GNU grep -oP over the same one-line subject.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t pcre) == builtin ]]; then
  pcre find-all '[0-9]+' 'rev2=8 rev19=204'
else
  printf '%s\n' 'rev2=8 rev19=204' | grep -oP '[0-9]+'
fi

cases.purpose: Pin the documented find-all iteration behavior for an empty alternative that can also consume a character: empty at offset zero, the non-empty retry, then empty at the end.
Compare PCRE alternation and digit matching across two fixture files, including GNU-compatible filename prefixes when multiple files are named.
cases.script:
printf 'ERR-12\nignore\n' > first.txt
printf 'WARN-7\nerr-8\n' > second.txt
if [[ $(type -t pcre) == builtin ]]; then
  pcre grep '^(?:ERR|WARN)-[0-9]+$' first.txt second.txt
else
  grep -P '^(?:ERR|WARN)-[0-9]+$' first.txt second.txt
fi

cases.purpose: Verify both line selectors return status 1 with no output and no diagnostic when a readable fixture file has no matching line.
cases.script:
printf 'one\ntwo\n' > lines.txt
if [[ $(type -t pcre) == builtin ]]; then
  pcre grep '^missing$' lines.txt
else
  grep -P '^missing$' lines.txt
fi

cases.purpose: Check documented -X byte transport and global substitution of a NUL byte: hex 610062 decodes to a NUL-delimited subject, 00 is replaced by ff, and output is lower-case hex.
Check malformed PCRE syntax fails with the documented command failure status and emits a diagnostic; diagnostic wording is implementation and PCRE2-version dependent.
Qualify immediate delivery of a matching line before the input producer closes.
cases.reason: The supplied runner starts each fixture with stdin connected to /dev/null and provides no producer-open FIFO or PTY observation hook. A future test requires a disposable VM or runner-provided private FIFO/PTY producer that writes one matching line, stays open, and lets the test assert that pcre grep emits the line before EOF. No operation is executed here.
